text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, articles, and websites. By studying patterns in this data, they learn to predict the next word in a sentence, which lets them generate human-like responses. When you give an LLM a prompt, you’re actually engineering the context to guide its answer—clear, specific instructions usually get better results. These models can write essays, summarize information, and even help with coding. However, they have limits. They don’t truly understand meaning, and they can make up facts or repeat biases found in their training data, so you should always double-check their output.
